title: TVS Motor Company Ltd - 532343 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TVS Motor Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR17,103 crores and PAT 52% to INR1,377 crores, alongside approval of a consumer finance demerger.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record volume (1.9 million units, up 27%), revenue, EBITDA and profit, with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 13.0%. Management said domestic 2W ICE and EV and 3W all grew faster than industry, and international sales hit a record 5.39 lakh units (up 35%). The Board approved a demerger of the consumer finance and related undertaking (including the TVS Credit Services stake) into a separate listed holding company, with shareholders receiving mirror shareholding; completion is expected around July 2027 appointed date after 8 to 10 months of approvals. Management guided to single-digit industry growth in H2 with base effects, and cost pressure expected to ease in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Domestic 2W
segments.commentary: Total 2W ICE sales grew 20% YoY vs industry 14%; domestic ICE up 16% vs industry 10%. Domestic 2W EV up 129% vs industry 84%. EV penetration of 2W was 11.6% in September (scooters about 22%).

segments.name: Domestic 3W
segments.commentary: ICE plus EV 3W volume about 26,300 units, up 65% from 16,000 vs industry 23%. EV penetration of 3W about 44% in Q2 and about 48% in September.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record 5.39 lakh units in H1, up 35% YoY; Q2 international 2W ICE up 33% vs industry 27%. International EV sales about 6,930 units in Q2 vs 1,726 last year. Africa was the key driver.

segments.name: TVS Credit (consumer finance)
segments.commentary: Book size INR33,818 crores, up 22% from INR27,807 crores; PBT INR330 crores, up 19% from INR277 crores. Network over 65,000 touch points; 14 lakh new customers in the quarter; customer base about 2.7 crores.

segments.name: Norton (e-bike)
segments.commentary: Manx R and Atlas launches under way in Europe (dealers in UK, Italy, France; Germany and Spain coming); India launch expected in coming months; US preparations underway. Current-quarter e-bike loss is lower than the prior quarter, though brand and launch costs rose.

guidance_outlook: Industry ICE growth in 2W and 3W expected to be single digit in H2 FY27 given the high base from Nov-Dec last year; management said it would wait a couple of weeks for a clearer Q3 view.
TVS expects to outgrow the industry in domestic and international markets in Q3 and Q4.
Material cost increases expected to be unlikely in Q3 and Q4 beyond small increases; Q4 may stabilise or soften.
Capacity: 2W capacity to exceed 8 million units and 3W to reach about 0.4 million soon; EV capacity at 60,000-65,000 units per month now, with plans for about 80,000.
Demerger appointed date is July 2027; approvals (regulatory, shareholder, NCLT) expected to take 8 to 10 months. Management to give FY28-FY29 investment guidance next quarter.
capex_capacity: EV capacity at about 60,000-65,000 units per month (domestic plus exports), with next-level expansion to about 80,000 planned and under way; Orbiter capacity to be enhanced in Q4.
2W capacity to cross 8 million units; 3W capacity to reach about 0.4 million soon.
Capacity expansion lead time for new models is about 3 months, per management.
Management said capacity planning for next year is starting now, given market pull and longer-range planning needs.

Additional INR1,200 crores equity infusion into TVS Credit Services is planned before the demerger, depending on capital requirements; INR711 crores was a secondary purchase of TVS Credit shares during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Dealer inventory held at 21-30 days (management said under 30 days, with many dealers under 21 days); cash-and-carry model.
Price actions: Q1 to Q2 material costs rose about 1.9% and selling prices rose 1.6%; small price increases taken early in Q3, with another review after Diwali.
EV industry grew about 75% in H1 per management; scooters share of category about 41% including EV, with ICE scooters at about 32-33%.
Ronin volume expected to go beyond 15,000 units, per management.
PLI benefit about 1.3-1.4% of turnover; management said the company has crossed the 10,000 cumulative mark and is on track for the higher incentive slab.

qa_highlights.question: How is TVS building EV capacity given supply constraints, and what is the Ronin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: EV industry grew about 75% in H1; capacity now 60,000-65,000 units/month, with 80,000 planned. Ronin is expected to go beyond 15,000 units per month, with new variants and a large capacity investment under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure of the consumer finance demerger and what holdings will TVS Motor keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Demerged undertaking includes the TVS Credit Services investment and some non-core investments, moved to a new company with mirror shareholding. TVS Motor keeps no stake; the TVS Credit business is not being merged into the new entity.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the demerger listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Post shareholder approval and NCLT process, around 8 to 10 months. The appointed date is July 2027, after the NBFC consolidation mandated by RBI (approvals expected by March or April 2027).

qa_highlights.question: What is the valuation and net worth of TVS Credit?
qa_highlights.answer: No valuation is set in a demerger. Net worth is about INR6,500 crores before the proposed INR1,200 crore equity infusion. Management declined to give ROE and ROA figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for industry growth in H2 and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-digit growth expected in Q3 given a high base. Material costs expected to rise less in Q3 and Q4; Q1 to Q2 prices rose 1.6% vs 1.9% material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: Are EV e-bike losses coming down outside Norton?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Norton e-mobility losses have been curtailed and will be cut further. The Norton loss is lower than in the prior quarter, but brand and launch costs rose.

risks_watch: Base effect in Nov-Dec: management flagged a high prior-year base, making H2 growth more cautious (single digit expected).
Commodity cost inflation: Q1 to Q2 material costs rose about 1.9%; price actions need to keep pace, and employee and marketing costs rose sharply.
Norton and the e-bike business continue to lose money; cumulative losses about INR1,300 crores over 4-5 years per an analyst; India launch and US plans still pending.
Demerger execution: 8 to 10 months to approvals, NBFC consolidation under RBI direction, and the July 2027 appointed date. Business split and valuation are not yet disclosed.
Next quarter: Q3 volume and EBITDA trends after Diwali, EV capacity ramp to 80,000, and FY28-29 investment guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and share gains; cautious on H2 industry growth due to base effects. Management was evasive on demerger valuation, ROE/ROA and EV unit economics, pointing to later disclosure.
key_quotes: we achieved the highest ever sales volume, revenue and profits.
Margin will continue to grow because when the top line is growing, I'm very sure that is going to also fall through into EBITDA journey.
I'm pretty confident that our products will do very well even the next year, financial year.
I'm of the view that I think we have to look at together scooters.

adds.what: 3W capacity to reach about 0.4 million units
EV capacity expansion to about 80,000 units per month from 60,000-65,000 currently

growth.why: No numeric revenue guide; management expects to outgrow the industry in Q3 and Q4 and EBITDA margin to keep improving, backed by 2W capacity above 8 million, 3W about 0.4 million and EV capacity moving from 60-65k to about 80k per month, though H2 industry growth was cut to single digit and no timeline was given for the EV step-up beyond FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin rose 30 bps to 13.0% from 12.7%, management is 'confident' of continued EBITDA momentum, and material cost increases are expected to be unlikely in Q3-Q4 beyond small rises, though Q1-Q2 material costs rose 1.9% vs selling prices up only 1.6%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 2W capacity to cross 8 million units (Q4 FY27 horizon), 3W to reach about 0.4 million soon, and EV capacity expansion from 60,000-65,000 to about 80,000 units per month is already under construction; Ronin capacity investment is under way.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects to outgrow the industry in Q3 and Q4 after Q2 volume rose 27% to 1.9 million units and international hit a record 5.39 lakh units in H1 (+35%), though H2 industry ICE growth is guided to single digit on a high Nov-Dec base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capacity planning for next year is starting now, a Rs1,200 crore equity infusion into TVS Credit is planned pre-demerger, and FY28-29 investment guidance is due next quarter; the 2W/3W/EV step-ups already under way make a further announcement probable though no amount has been named.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Industry H2 growth was cut to single digit (Q3 'good single-digit') on a high base, so the call does not point to raised guidance even though TVS expects to outgrow the industry.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 industry ICE growth guided to single digit on base effects and commodity costs rose 1.9% in Q1-Q2 against 1.6% price increases, so a softer Q3 print is a risk if pricing lags.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Norton Manx R and Atlas are launching in Europe with Germany and Spain to follow, India launch expected in coming months, and US preparations are under way; Ronin volume is expected beyond 15,000 units.

rows.label: Consumer finance demerger into separate listed holdco
rows.why: Board approved demerger of TVS Credit stake with mirror shareholding; approvals (regulatory, shareholder, NCLT) expected to take 8-10 months, with TVS Credit book at Rs33,818 crore (+22%) and PBT Rs330 crore (+19%).

rows.label: E-bike loss reduction outside Norton
rows.why: Non-Norton e-mobility losses have been curtailed and will be cut further, and the Norton loss is lower than the prior quarter, though brand and launch costs rose and cumulative losses are about Rs1,300 crore per an analyst.

rows.label: Post-Diwali price review
rows.why: Small price increases taken early in Q3 with another review after Diwali, to offset Q1-Q2 material cost rise of about 1.9% against a 1.6% selling price rise.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume, share gains and EBITDA momentum and cautious on H2 industry growth due to base effects; analysts probed the demerger valuation, ROE/ROA and EV unit economics, which management largely deferred.
